patient.chief_complaint: EMS called to college party - 19yo found convulsing continuously, unknown drug ingestion, 15 minutes
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Garcia is a 19-year-old college freshman with no medical history who is brought by EMS from a college party where he was found convulsing continuously for approximately 15 minutes. His friends report he ingested an unknown pill approximately 60-90 minutes before the seizure onset — they believe it may have been sold as 'Molly' (MDMA) but acknowledge they are not certain what it was. He had also consumed approximately 4-5 alcoholic drinks during the evening. He has absolutely no prior history of seizures. He has no medical conditions and takes no medications. On EMS arrival he was in continuous generalized tonic-clonic activity with severe agitation and hyperthermia. Temperature on EMS arrival was 39.6°C. The differential for new-onset SE in a young person at a party with unknown drug ingestion includes: (1) stimulant toxidrome (MDMA, amphetamines, cocaine) with sympathomimetic crisis and possible hyponatremia, (2) isoniazid toxicity (rare but causes pyridoxine-deficient SE refractory to benzodiazepines), (3) tricyclic antidepressant (TCA) overdose causing seizures and QRS widening, (4) gamma-hydroxybutyrate (GHB) causing CNS depression then paradoxical seizures on withdrawal, (5) fentanyl-contaminated drug causing hypoxic seizures. Blood toxicology must be sent immediately. The unknown pill and party context make TCA overdose a critical consideration given the wide QRS and the difficulty in treating TCA-related SE.
